subject: DNS and certificate handover for private inference endpoints

Subject: Proposal: hybrid DNS delegation + cert handshake for private endpoints

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Acme CloudOps will be standing up a VPC-private endpoint for the Redwood inference appliances in our co-lo region. A few constraints from our side:

- We want split-horizon DNS so customer-facing names resolve to the public layer, internal service names resolve to the private endpoints.
- We need a documented certificate handoff pattern so our ops team can renew certs for the private hostnames without exposing keys.
- We must preserve SNI for multi-tenant proxying (we run an L4/L7 front proxy) and prefer to avoid TLS termination in the customer network if Redwood's dedicated proxy can handle mTLS to the runtime.

Can you share a proposed runbook and the minimal artifacts you need from Acme (namespaces, delegated zone, CSR behavior, ACME account options)? We've got a firewall maintenance window next week so would like to align timelines.

Attached is a short network diagram from our infra team (stubs).

Thanks,
Luis Ortega
Edge Platforms Lead, Acme CloudOps

Attachment: acme-brief-network-stub.png

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: luis.ortega@acme-cloudops.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Bcc: 
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: hybrid DNS delegation + cert handshake for private endpoints

Luis — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram.

High level proposal from Redwood:

1) Zone delegation model: Acme delegates a sub-zone (e.g. private.redwood.acme.internal) to Redwood-managed DNS servers inside their VPC via NS records. This gives us control of records for runtime hostnames while keeping the parent zone with Acme. If full delegation is not possible, we'll accept a small set of CNAMEs per host.

2) Certificate model: We prefer issuing short-lived certs (7–14 days) from Redwood's internal CA for the runtime side, and use an ACME flow with an automated CSR signing agent operating in Acme's VPC. That agent holds a per-instance private key and performs CSR validation using a mutually-agreed token exchange over a secure control channel.

3) TLS termination and SNI: Preferred path is to keep TLS to the runtime (i.e., TLS passthrough at the Acme proxy) and let Redwood terminate at our runtime if you provision an L4 pass-through. If Acme must terminate (for visibility), then we request a proxying certificate model where Acme's proxy presents a frontend cert and forwards traffic to Redwood over mTLS. We'll provide a documented fallback that uses a short-lived cert on the proxy.

4) Operational runbook and artifacts: see attached draft runbook (redwood-acme-handover-runbook-draft.pdf). Minimal items we need from Acme: delegated NS records or CNAME map, ACL for the control agent IPs, and a service account + KMS fingerprint for encrypting rotation tokens.

Proposed timeline: runbook review (this week), test handoff in staging (next week), production handover during your firewall window (two weeks out).

Action items:
- Luis: confirm if delegation (NS) is acceptable or if you prefer CNAMEs.
- Monica: can you review the runbook section on token exchange?
- Sergio: please sanity-check the SNI/proxy constraints for multi-tenant routing.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-acme-handover-runbook-draft.pdf

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: hybrid DNS delegation + cert handshake for private endpoints

Thanks Karthik and Luis — quick notes from the runtime/proxy side.

On delegation vs CNAMEs:
- Full NS delegation is operationally cleaner for frequent updates (autoscaling host registration). If Acme has security concerns, CNAMEs per host are acceptable but we need an automated provisioning API to avoid manual TTL churn.

On certs and ACME agent:
- We'll ship a small signing agent (container) that runs in Acme's VPC and talks to Redwood's control plane over a mutually-authenticated channel. The agent stores private keys in the customer's KMS (customer-managed) and only sends CSRs to Redwood for signing. Keys never leave the customer's vault.
- For clients that require SNI at the proxy: proxy presents the frontend cert, then we require TLS re-origin to Redwood over mTLS. To avoid double-termination pitfalls, we recommend:
  - Use proxy SNI routing to route to the correct backend cluster.
  - Preserve the client SNI header for logging/tracing, do not rewrite unless necessary.

SNI/proxy constraints (attachment: sni-proxy-constraints.md) — includes: acceptable cipher suites, minimum TLS version (1.3 preferred), and header preservation rules.

Security ask: we will need Acme to add our control-plane IPs to your egress allowlist for the agent handshake and to provide a KMS public key fingerprint.

Next steps: Luis — can you confirm whether your infra team can run the signing agent (container) and share a contact for KMS integration? If so, we'll schedule a short runbook walkthrough with ops and security.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
